01.r: A new ruler takes the throne.
01.n: A perfect with 'and', carrying the vision forward into the future. STEPBible tags this occurrence with the sense 'rise'; BDB lists 'come into being' among the verb's senses. YLT renders the form literally as a past.

02.r: Taking the position of the king before him.
02.n: Literally 'on' or 'upon' his place, as YLT's 'on his station' keeps it.

03.r: The place of the ruler who has just fallen.
03.n: BDB: base, pedestal, office; the brief's lexicon includes 'office, place, estate'. The KJV's 'estate' means his standing or position.

s: one who causes to pass through
04.r: The new ruler sends an agent through his realm.
04.n: A participle of the causative form of 'to pass over': one who makes someone pass through. JPS and ASV keep it, 'cause ... to pass through'.
t: one that shall cause ... to pass through
one that shall cause ... to pass through

05.r: An official who presses the people for payment.
05.n: Our register renders this participle 'taskmaster'. Gesenius: to impel, to urge, to drive, and also to demand a debt or to demand tribute; the brief's lexicon includes 'exactor of tribute' for the participle. Here it most likely means a collector who presses for tribute; JPS and YLT say 'exactor', the BSB 'tax collector'.

06.r: Through the finest part of the kingdom.
06.n: Gesenius: ornament, and he cites this verse: sending the exactor through the glory of the kingdom, which he takes to mean Palestine, the most excellent part of the kingdom. He adds that some take the word as tribute, but does not follow them. There is no preposition in the Hebrew; 'through' is carried by the verb 'cause to pass'.

07.n: Gesenius: kingdom, royal dominion, a word of the later Hebrew. There is no article in the Hebrew: 'of a kingdom'. The DRC reads the phrase differently, 'unworthy of kingly honour'.

08.r: Marks how soon his end will come.

09.n: The plural of 'one': 'days, ones', meaning a few days.

10.n: Gesenius: to break, to break to pieces; this is the passive form, to be broken. Every translation here says 'destroyed'.

11.r: His fall is not by the usual means.

12.r: Not by the anger of an enemy or a mob.
12.n: Gesenius: properly the nose, the member with which one breathes, and from the snorting of the enraged, anger. The form is dual, 'nostrils'.

_extra.2: ἐκ (from): begins a phrase in the Greek, 'from his root a shoot of the kingdom', which the Hebrew of this verse does not have.
_extra.3: τῆς (the): part of the added phrase.
_extra.4: ῥίζης (root): part of the added phrase.
_extra.5: αὐτοῦ (his): part of the added phrase.
_extra.6: φυτὸν (plant, shoot): part of the added phrase.
_extra.7: τῆς (the): part of the added phrase.
_extra.8: βασιλείας (of the kingdom): part of the added phrase.

01.n: ἀνίστημι, to rise up, to arise.

03.n: ἑτοιμασία, readiness, a prepared place: the Greek reads 'upon his place'.

04.n: παραβιβάζω, to make pass by or through.

05.n: πράσσω, to do, to exact: the Greek has 'one exacting', where the Hebrew has 'a taskmaster'.

09.n: ἐκείναις, 'those': the Greek says 'in those days', not 'in a few days'.

10.n: συντρίβω, to crush, to break in pieces, as the Hebrew.

12.n: πρόσωπον, face: the Greek takes the Hebrew word in its sense of 'face' rather than 'anger'.
